Moves Card Program To Blockchain Settlement
This enables transactions through SoFiUSD on Mastercard’s global payments network under the companies’ partnership announced in March.
SoFi Bank is moving its entire $25 billion card program to stablecoin-based transaction settlement using SoFiUSD.
Read Also:  Buying SOFI Is Like Buying 'AMD or Nvidia' at the Bottom: Strategists Highlight Bold Bull Case for SoFi Technologies

SoFiUSD is the first stablecoin issued by a nationally chartered bank and is designed to maintain a 1:1 redemption value against the U.S. dollar and is backed primarily by cash reserves. Transactions are now live on the blockchain.

The launch gives card issuers, acquirers and merchants another way to manage settlement and liquidity through established payment infrastructure while supporting broader use of bank-issued stablecoins in payments.
It also demonstrates how bank-issued stablecoins can work alongside existing payment networks to connect traditional financial systems with blockchain-based infrastructure.

The bigger overhang remains the longer trend, with shares still 11.6% below the 200-day SMA and down 42.49% over the past 12 months.

Momentum looks more range-bound than trending right now, with RSI at 45.17 (neutral), which typically signals neither buyers nor sellers have strong control.
